The main takeaway from our work is that
LC-MS-based SUSAs are able to detect the intake of the tryptamines 5-Me-2-Me-O-DALT, 2-Me-O-ALCHT, and 2-Me-DIP, which are not detectable by GC-MS-based SUSA.
the metabolites of the studied N,N-dialkytryptamines can be detected in urine samples by LC-MS SUSAS.

LC-MS-based SUSAs might be more sensitive than the GC-MS-based SUSA for the detection of tryptamine-derived compounds and that their phase I and phase II metabolites might serve as biomarkers for the detection and quantification of these new psychoactive substances in urine.
